38: Traits in one place, with clearer descriptions
39: The full trait overview lets you browse discovered dispositions and titles and read their descriptions. Distinct grade colors, title colors, and description formatting help you make training decisions.
42: Cryo cells display each character's face and name. Browse through pages to find someone in storage, with less need to search a list from memory alone.
44: The tutorial now uses the latest shared layout. Expanded descriptions of places and people help you understand where you are and whom you've met.
48: Expanded regional and facility backgrounds, major character art and portraits, full-body combat art, and defeat scenes. This complete edition brings together base-game, Indie Patch, personal, and additional artwork.
51: Replacement background used in the 2.4 series
53: A comparison of the previous and replacement backgrounds for the same location. The image on the left is the previous asset, not a screenshot of version 2.3.
55: Each setting has its own atmosphere: a misty forest at the Fog Border, a spectator-lined arena, and a torchlit underground fighting pit at the Catfight Club.
56: Monsters in scale, characters in arms
57: Composition and backgrounds convey the size of giant enemies, while smaller foes are scaled to the surrounding terrain. Major characters' weapons and combat appearances have been brought in line with their established roles.
58: Combat and defeat as a set
59: Full-body combat art is paired with defeat scenes, and group opponents have scenes showing their defeat together. Some monsters also have distinct appearances at different growth stages.
63: There are new ways to enjoy the artwork, too.
64: Switch between registered original and alternate images and keep your selection. You can also hide the UI to view cutscenes on their own. This edition brings together the selected assets; it does not replace every image with new artwork.
67: and whom will you send into battle?
68: The changes in 2.4 go beyond the screen. Companion combat, individual growth and dialogue, and the choices involved in managing several characters build on the existing flow of training, deliveries, and battles.
69: Send a slave or assistant into Fog Border combat first
70: On ordinary Fog Border patrols, you can send one companion into battle first. If they lose, the player character takes over. Damage already dealt, defeated enemies, and resources the enemies have spent are preserved. Each combatant chooses equipment when their turn begins.

76: Damage dealt to enemies is preserved
77: This does not send the slave, assistant, and player character into battle in a three-person sequence. Check your companion's condition and action points, and remember that defeat has consequences.
81: Personality shapes learning speed, repeated activities, reactions to achievement, and even how unpleasant experiences are remembered. Not every disposition is visible from the start; some traits are discovered through activities.
83: Differences in learning speed and growth

93: A distinct kind of staying power in battle
94: Track changes through the full trait overview and discovery notices, and manage characters with Constitution Improvement, Chaotic Essence, and more. Special qualities such as Versatile, Peerless Beauty, and Meiki also add value to training and trading.
96: An information panel for browsing attributes and traits
97: Meeting Isabella, updated to match her current appearance
100: Conversation topics now cover the past, impressions, requests, desired activities, dislikes, current mood, and opinions of other characters. Replies vary with personality, speech style, relationships, emotions, and recent experiences.
101: Recently used wording repeats less often, and longer replies are grouped so that sentences are not cut in the middle. Unique characters' stories and manually written backgrounds are preserved.
102: Dialogue combines predefined passages to fit the situation. It does not mean thousands of standalone events or unlimited conversation.
104: Battle experience earned by the characters who actually fight, witness accounts from the Fog Border, and Rally and Catfight Club results now contribute to personal reputation. The results of training show beyond the lesson menus.
105: Manage several characters across rooms and tasks
106: Choose a diet for each private room and distinguish shared chores from a private-room maid's duties. Navigation between rooms and storage has also been refined to make characters easier to find.
109: and the choices you make each day.
110: How you train a character, where you trade, and how you spend your action points now connect more clearly.
111: Key adjustments you'll notice in play
116: Base action points adjusted for physical fitness; reduced overwork strain for muscular characters
117: Consider physical training alongside the way you divide up the day's tasks.
119: Constitution traits now affect combat resources and physical training, with improved growth effects
120: The same schedule can lead to different training choices depending on a character's constitution.
122: Trade value reflects current attributes, skills, obedience, overall grade, and special traits
123: Training results and individual strengths matter when deciding to sell.
125: Existing prize tiers increased by the same proportion; results and prize announcements combined
126: Review the match result and prize money together.
128: Payment caps removed on Easy and Normal; Hardcore retains caps and explains deductions
129: Auction payment rules depend on your chosen difficulty.
130: Buyer rumors suited to your characters
131: Local contacts can share buyer rumors suited to the characters you own. When there is no suitable special recommendation, they point you toward a Guild buyback.
132: Trades that recognize a character's value
133: Improved the value of Meiki, Peerless Beauty, and Versatile, along with some special trading benefits. NPCs do not all use the same price multiplier; a customer's requirements and available funds still matter.
134: A crisis screen for reviewing assets and options when cash runs short
135: Ways to respond to a financial crisis
136: A new sequence lets you respond to a shortage of funds by selling assets or raising money yourself. Housing, decorations, facilities, and owned characters have separate disposal and settlement processes.
137: You'll need to decide what to keep and what to sell. Actually disposing of a character also has consequences for ongoing quests tied to them.
141: New artwork is accompanied by connections between match choices, results, and follow-up scenes. Existing major events also have updated presentation to match current appearances and locations.
142: After victory, decide your opponent's fate
143: Regular Colosseum matches and ordinary Catfight Club matches lead to a choice to execute or spare your opponent. Artwork and dialogue reflect your decision, while practice matches end as sparring sessions, separate from fights over life and death.
144: Your conduct can come back to you
145: Acts of cruelty and mercy build a history. This also affects how opponents treat your characters when they lose in the Colosseum or Catfight Club. The risk of injury in combat still remains.

149: Distinct scenes for victory, defeat, and what follows
150: Separate outcomes cover sparring by the player character, slave, or assistant; death, execution, and the evacuation of survivors in regular matches; the defeated opponent's fate; and scenes after becoming champion. Result dialogue has also been refined to connect the finished battle naturally with the next scene.
151: Isabella's tavern and recruitment scenes now match her current appearance, and combat artwork for Egeya and other major event opponents has been improved. Sequential scenes in the red-light district and salon, plus role outfits for some unique characters, have also been refined.
154: The Portal Guardian and Vatican Paladin show how introductions and combat presentation have been updated for existing events. They do not indicate newly unlocked regions or separate quests.
